items.title: 67460_Sammy Price oral history interview
items.q: This is where I first met Oscar Pettiford.

ctx.x:
PRICE: 5.
DM: 25...
PRICE: 1925. Then I by this time was very, very close to Ella B. Moore. Well, I could dance and this gave me the opportunity--she had a little amateur show of kids; they were pretty good, though, you know, do little drama things and chorus girls and, you know--so in 1925 she said to me, "Willie, you know I think you're going to be a musician." Right then I says, "Why?" She says, "I hear you always fooling around." Wherever I saw a piano--they were so rare there--that wherever I saw one I ran…

at the theater when they come and I would stay until they left. I watched everything and tried to just be a professional person in that way. And then, actually I was improving on my piano playing. And people would let me play now that...around at the house-rent parties I was, you know, popular. Very popular. That was in 1925, and I went up...we went up to Okmulgee, Oklahoma. This is where I first met Oscar Pettiford.
